data.narrative:
Xona Space Systems is a Series C-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $281M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 private-sector comps at the same stage (Sierra Space, Varda Space Industries, Skyryse) and 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two quantitative methods are applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $281M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $478M. The peer-median approach uses three same-sector, same-stage private companies trading at a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures. A public-sector P/S median of 23.9x exists across six space and aerospace tickers but remains inapplicable without target revenue data.

Triangulating these two methods yields a valuation range of $406M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $989M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around growth trajectory and competitive positioning within a heterogeneous peer set. The range's upper bound is anchored by peer-median findings; the lower bound reflects earlier-stage financial metrics. Key uncertainties include revenue scale, unit economics, and whether Xona's technology or market position justifies positioning toward the upper or lower quartile of the peer distribution.
